The compromised actions-cool GitHub Actions were re-enabled in September with malicious tags and ran the payload again

On 2026-05-18 all 53 version tags of the actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action, and all 15 of actions-cool/maintain-one-comment, were moved to imposter commits whose payload reads the Runner.Worker process memory for decrypted workflow secrets and sends them over HTTPS to an attacker-controlled domain (StepSecurity); Socket places the compromise in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. GitHub disabled both repositories on 2026-05-19 but they became reachable again on 2026-09-16 with the malicious tags intact, so tag-referencing workflows ran the payload again and SafeDep counted six newly infected repositories by 2026-09-24, until GitHub disabled both again by 2026-09-25 (Socket, The Hacker News). Only workflows pinned to a full commit SHA from before 2026-05-18 were unaffected.

The campaign (active since early 2025, attributed by CrowdStrike to likely Russia-based operators on the basis of CIS-locale exit checks) used Solana blockchain memo fields, BitTorrent DHT, Google Calendar event titles, and traditional VPS C2 in parallel for resilience; takedown required cutting all four at once. It began as an arbitrary-file-upload-to-RCE cluster (CWE-434) surfaced by researcher mySites.guru via source-code audits: JoomShaper SP Page Builder (CVE-2026-48908), Joomlack Page Builder CK (CVE-2026-56290), Balbooa Forms (CVE-2026-56291), iCagenda (CVE-2026-48939), RSFiles! The operator ran DeepSeek behind the open-source Hermes Agent for fully autonomous target enumeration and exploitation against seven CVEs and more than 460 targets, and every autonomous exploitation attempt failed, defeated only by target-side configuration. objects.description: Storm-2945's primary persistent Windows implant, written in Go and delivered by the CaptiveCrunch captive-portal lures. Runs first in dropper mode behind a configurable fake progress window imitating Windows Update, a security scan or a redistributable installer, then registers as a Windows service masquerading as a cloud-sync utility. Establishes redundant persistence across service registration, Registry Run keys and scheduled tasks with a watchdog that restores anything defenders remove; command and control uses ephemeral ECDH P-256 key exchange with SHA-256 session-key derivation over a custom JSON protocol. Collection covers keylogging, clipboard, screenshots, microphone and webcam capture, removable media, browser credential theft and an eighteen-category host security-posture sweep (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-07-31).

objects.description: Storm-2945's in-memory PowerShell infostealer, deployed alongside CornFlake in the CaptiveCrunch operation for high-volume theft of browser session cookies, saved passwords, Microsoft 365 SSO tokens and Wi-Fi credentials. Disables AMSI via .NET reflection, performs a timing-based sandbox check, and escalates through three silent UAC-bypass techniques in ordered fallback before reverting to a visible prompt. Defeats Chrome App-Bound Encryption both by impersonating a SYSTEM token and by driving the browser's own DevTools Protocol, and collects Microsoft 365 and Azure AD access, refresh and Web Account Manager tokens from the Token Broker cache, enabling SSO session replay without browser cookies (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-07-31).

Microsoft Threat Intelligence disclosed CaptiveCrunch on 2026-07-31, a campaign it attributes to Storm-2945, assessed as an operational sub-cluster of the SVR-attributed actor Midnight Blizzard. Since early May 2026 the actor has manipulated DNS and HTTP traffic on hospitality networks served by captive portals worldwide, redirecting users through its own infrastructure and answering browser connectivity checks with ClickFix-style fake browser and OS update prompts. The payloads are CornFlake, a Go Windows RAT with redundant persistence and a watchdog that restores anything defenders remove, and ChocoShell, an in-memory PowerShell stealer that takes browser cookies, saved passwords, Microsoft 365 SSO tokens and Wi-Fi credentials. Since 16 July some landing pages also drive Entra ID device-code phishing. Travelling government and diplomatic staff are named target populations.

objects.description:
A Joomla anti-spam plugin hands unserialize() an attacker-controlled object on every public form, reaching code execution on Joomla cores up to 5.2.1

VulnCheck disclosed CVE-2026-65883 on 2026-07-30, an unauthenticated PHP object injection in the Aimy Captcha-Less Form Guard plugin for Joomla, versions 18.0 through 20.0 and fixed in 20.1. The plugin base64-decodes a hidden form token, runs it through a repeating-key XOR and passes the result straight to unserialize() with no signature and no allowed_classes, and because the plugin renders a ciphertext for that same keystream in every protected form, the key is recoverable and the object forgeable. On Joomla 3.9 through 5.2.1 it chains through a core gadget to remote code execution as the web user. No exploitation is reported, but three other unauthenticated Joomla extension flaws disclosed this year were exploited in the wild and KEV-listed.

objects.description:
The Joomla page builder whose icon-upload zero-day was exploited in June ships four more flaws, one reads the whole database without an account

mySites.guru disclosed four vulnerabilities in JoomShaper's SP Page Builder 6.7.0 on 2026-07-27, all fixed the same day in 6.7.1, with four CVEs assigned by the Joomla CNA and a fifth (CVE-2026-65876, 9.2, an unauthenticated SQL injection the discloser did not report or test) covering the same versions, so 6.7.1 fixes five issues, not four. CVE-2026-65766 (Joomla CNA, CVSS 4.0 9.2) places a request value straight into the ORDER BY clause of the Dynamic Content endpoint's query; the only control in front of it is a Joomla CSRF token, which Joomla issues to every anonymous visitor on page load, so a scripted attacker fetches a token and replays it, effectively pre-authentication SQL injection that reads the entire Joomla database, password hashes included. CVE-2026-65879 is a design flaw rather than a slip: the contact-form addons sign the configured recipient address with a secret hardcoded identically into every shipped copy of the extension, so anyone holding the extension can forge a signature and send mail to any recipient with a spoofed sender through the site's own mail server. The same extension's unauthenticated icon-upload zero-day was being exploited in the wild in June 2026.

objects.content: This pipeline's 2026-07-21 entry has Searchlight Cyber's Adam Kues tasking GPT5.6 "to autonomously rediscover and weaponise the already-patched" WordPress WP2Shell chain, and the W30 weekly carried the same framing. The cited Searchlight Cyber post says the opposite: the model was pointed at the WordPress source and explicitly forbidden from diffing against a patched version or using changelogs and git history, and Searchlight then "held off on publishing this issue to give defenders a chance to upgrade their WordPress instances over the weekend". This pipeline's own 2026-07-18 entry already named Searchlight Cyber as the discoverer of CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137. The correction matters because it changes the capability claim: not an LLM reconstructing a known, patched bug, but an LLM finding a pre-authentication RCE in WordPress core that no one had published, whose disclosure produced the out-of-band 7.0.2 / 6.9.5 / 6.8.6 release.

The 2026-07-31 entry here on Unit 42's autonomous-AI intrusion campaign framed the operation as landing three confirmed compromises, all from the operator's manual NetScaler work, and supported it with an evidence quote attributed to Unit 42 that does not appear in Unit 42's post. The real sentence records data exfiltration from three Citrix NetScaler targets (CVE-2026-3055) AND command execution on 11 Marimo notebook endpoints (CVE-2026-39987), and Unit 42's own CVE table lists CVE-2026-39987 with command execution confirmed. Two further CVEs carry confirmed attempts: reverse shells against nine Apache Tomcat servers (CVE-2026-34486) and callbacks from three IKE VPN endpoints (CVE-2026-33824). The operational consequence is an exposure list four CVEs long rather than one, with Marimo Notebook the addition most likely to be missing from an asset inventory.

objects.description:
Swiss federal SharePoint servers breached mid-patching, ~200 accounts taken, servers now being rebuilt

The Bundesamt für Informatik und Telekommunikation (BIT), which runs the Swiss Confederation's own data centres, disclosed on 2026-08-04 that its on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Servers were compromised by unknown actors, presumably through the SharePoint flaws Microsoft disclosed in mid-July 2026, and that the credentials of roughly 200 accounts (user accounts and technical service accounts) were taken. BIT had begun installing the July updates immediately after release; staff spotted anomalies on 28 July and confirmed credential compromise on 31 July. Passwords were reset, internet access to SharePoint is blocked for non-federal users, and the affected servers are being rebuilt from scratch rather than patched in place.

objects.description: Elastic Security Labs' designation for an npm supply-chain worm wave identified on 2026-08-04 that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and backdoored over 400 packages totalling more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads. CHAINDROP executes from a package.json preinstall hook via a downloaded Bun runtime, harvests over 300 credential patterns including AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes secrets, self-propagates only through npm tokens that can publish without two-factor authentication, and resolves its exfiltration endpoint from an Ethereum smart contract at runtime. Elastic frames it as the return of the Shai-Hulud lineage rather than a new family (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-08-06).

objects.description: The canton's IT-office head states it could be the same vulnerability identified at federal level, a stated possibility, not a confirmed technical link

A second Swiss public-sector SharePoint victim in 48 hours, and the intrusion sat unnoticed for a week

The IT office of the Swiss canton of Graubünden disclosed on 2026-08-05 (one day after Switzerland's federal IT provider BIT disclosed an intrusion into its own on-premises SharePoint estate) that a SharePoint server hosting the cantonal administration's public web presence was compromised on the afternoon of 29 July 2026. Two files were placed on the cantonal server but their code was not executed, and a first analysis found no compromised accounts and no data exfiltration; confidential and specially-protected personal data are not held on those servers. The canton's IT chief says it could be the same vulnerability found at federal level, but neither Swiss disclosure names a CVE, and the canton shipped an out-of-band update on the evening of 5 August.
objects.name: Canton Graubünden discloses a SharePoint server breach a day after the Confederation did; the on-premises wave has reached Swiss cantonal government

objects.description:
A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain

Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns (AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens) and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.

objects.description: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability affecting versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated caller injects arbitrary SQL against the application database via the /api/session/reset_password endpoint and obtains administrator access to the instance, exposing stored credentials for connected databases and any data reachable through them. Assigned CVE-2026-72898 (CVSS 10.0) and added to CISA KEV on 2026-08-11. Framework and Tally confirmed data theft first (2026-08-03); VenariX tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents as of its 2026-08-24 update and attributes two self-hosted cases (Statista, Dodo Payments) to the Dire Wolf extortion group, with no evidence it found the flaw or is behind the rest.
objects.name: Metabase unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day exploitation (August 2026)

objects.description:
Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded

Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally confirmed customer data was taken from instances accessed on 2026-08-03. The flaw had no CVE identifier at disclosure; it is now tracked as CVE-2026-72898, which CISA added to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.
objects.name: Metabase CVE-2026-72898: an unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day gave attackers administrator access to BI instances, exploited since at least 2 August, with VenariX counting fifteen downstream victims

objects.description:
Cisco confirms exploitation of an unauthenticated ASA/FTD VPN denial-of-service flaw; hardening releases now replace the hot fixes, with no workaround

Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-20349 on 2026-08-11 and states its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in August 2026. Insufficient error checking when the Remote Access SSL VPN service parses HTTP requests lets an unauthenticated remote attacker send one crafted request and force the device to reload. Any ASA or FTD device with SSL listen sockets enabled is affected (IKEv2 remote access with client services, SSL VPN, or Zero Trust Network Access) across ASA 9.16 to 9.24 and FTD 7.0 to 10.0; Secure Firewall Management Center is not affected. There are no workarounds. The hot fixes Cisco first shipped have been superseded by hardening releases (ASA 9.16.4.103 to 9.24.1.26, FTD 7.0.10 to 10.0.2), which Cisco now recommends. CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog the same day with a 14 August deadline.

VulnCheck caught exploitation of the Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050; all four variants affected, V4.3.4-1 fixes

Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 of 2026-08-11 discloses CVE-2026-58115, rated 10.0 on both CVSS 3.1 and 4.0: SIMATIC IoT2050 devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, so an unauthenticated attacker with network reach can create a flow and run code with maximum privileges. Siemens' advisory, revised on 2026-11-04, lists the Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants, all versions below V4.3.4-1; V4.3.4-1 is the fix, and Siemens offers uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as interim mitigations. VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught exploitation, a single request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; the target was a canary and the activity looks like opportunistic mass scanning.

objects.description: Recorded Future's designation for the North Korean IT-worker cluster, a state-directed network of covert technology workers who pose as independent contractors and job-seeking developers to obtain remote employment, with earnings funnelled back through layered individual accounts. Insikt Group states the group overlaps with the vendor designations Jasper Sleet, UNC5267, Wagemole and Famous Chollima. Between late 2024 and early 2025 one cluster applied to over 1,100 companies, at times 60 positions a day, running at least 22 fabricated personas, some of which Insikt records as supported by AI-generated profile photographs from a face-swapping service, identity documents from an illicit document-generation service and purpose-configured chatbot assistants used to answer interview questions in real time, alongside fabricated code-hosting contribution histories; Insikt assesses the operators were highly likely employed by at least ten organisations. Employer-issued laptops are physically held by facilitators and worked remotely over commercial remote-desktop software with a commercial VPN marketed for circumventing China's national firewall, and Insikt places many operators' nexus in Shenyang, China. Roughly 80% of target companies were North American but operators applied in every region of the world (Insikt Group, 2026-08-18).

objects.description:
The precondition is wider than the headline version numbers suggest; on older builds a Gateway or AAA vserver alone is enough

Citrix published a bulletin on 2026-08-19 covering two NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway flaws, relayed the same day by CERT-EU as advisory 2026-010. CVE-2026-19490 is an authentication bypass using an alternate path, scored 9.3, against appliances configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or as an AAA virtual server; CVE-2026-19489 is a memory overflow reachable only where SIP ALG is enabled on a Large Scale NAT group. The exposure boundary is the operationally important part: on 14.1-43.56 and 13.1-61.28 and later the bypass applies only when a SAML action is configured, but on earlier builds and on 13.1 FIPS any Gateway or AAA virtual server configuration is enough. Fixed in 14.1-73.32, 13.1-63.21, 14.1-73.32 FIPS and 13.1-37.277. A public proof-of-concept appeared around 2026-09-03, exploitation attempts followed the same day, and CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog on 2026-09-09.

objects.description:
Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming

Zimbra shipped ZCS 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 with a fix for a command injection in the SNMP monitoring component, and the identifier CVE-2026-73570 followed on 2026-08-13. Microsoft Threat Intelligence now reports confirmed intrusions in more than one region and industry, with probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before disclosure, and CISA lists the flaw in KEV (added 2026-08-21). The flaw needs no authentication and applies only where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled; Microsoft's cases combined web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, so an upgrade does not evict an attacker already inside. CSIRT Italia reports that exploitation of this flaw has also led to ELock-family ransomware, cryptomining and theft of the LDAP database and credential hashes on exposed servers, and found no intrusion on regularly updated instances.

objects.description: Compromise of the Landesnetz, the shared network of the Berlin state administration, established by forensic investigation and confirmed by the Senate Chancellery on 2026-08-17; two Senate departments were isolated from the network from 2026-08-14 and reconnected on 2026-08-23, blocking housing-benefit disbursement to more than 50,000 entitled households and other district-level citizen services. The Landeskriminalamt, the Berlin public prosecutor and the BSI are involved. Investigative journalism (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28) first named a phishing-email click as the access vector and reported an extortion demand of 30 Bitcoin from a group media reporting attributes to Rhysida; Germany's BSI (BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04) describes the TerminalFix campaign and attributes Rhysida to a group it tracks as Vice Spider; heise reads BSI's Mastodon post of the same day as confirming TerminalFix as the Berlin vector, BSI told rbb24 on 2026-10-21 it does not confirm that link, and Berlin's Senate administration itself still declines to confirm either.

objects.name: GraphSpy

objects.description:
Dead-drop C2 moved from novelty to routine, and the control is an egress baseline rather than a blocklist

Red Canary's monthly threat round-up, published 2026-08-20 on July 2026 telemetry, records four new entrants to its most-prevalent list (GraphSpy, Phexia, CastleRAT and EtherRAT) of which three resolve their command-and-control address from a dead drop rather than from a hardcoded domain, and two of those three read it from a public blockchain smart contract. The technique defeats domain and IP blocking because the operator rewrites the contract value and every installation picks up the change. The fourth, GraphSpy, is an open-source Entra ID and Microsoft 365 attack tool with a browser GUI that centralises device-code phishing, primary refresh token theft, Windows Hello for Business key registration and MFA method manipulation, the third device-code phishing tool to reach that list in 2026.

objects.description: Previously unidentified modular loader documented by Expel on 2026-08-20, delivered by Microsoft Teams message from a company-styled onmicrosoft.com address impersonating the target's IT service desk and installed as an MSI presented as a 'PowerShell Cleaner' hosted on Azure blob storage. Six modules blending Python, PowerShell, C# and C++: a system profiler counting AD-joined computers, an in-memory DLL loader, PhishLocker (a counterfeit Windows lock screen harvesting the domain password), TrafficRedirector (a backconnect proxy defeating IP allow-listing), an interactive shell, and an outbound screen-streaming module. Expel assesses at low-to-medium confidence that it belongs to a ransomware group or an access broker selling to one (Expel, 2026-08-20).
objects.name: SynkLoader

objects.description:
SynkLoader pairs a fake Windows lock screen with a backconnect proxy, so the stolen domain password is used from the victim's own address

Expel documented SynkLoader on 2026-08-20, a previously unidentified loader delivered by Microsoft Teams message from a company-styled onmicrosoft.com address impersonating the target's own IT service desk, which talks the user into installing an MSI presented as a "PowerShell Cleaner" hosted on Azure blob storage. Six modules blend Python, PowerShell, C# and C++, some using three languages at once: a system profiler that counts Active Directory-joined computers, an in-memory DLL loader, PhishLocker (a counterfeit Windows lock screen that harvests the domain password), TrafficRedirector (a backconnect proxy), an interactive shell, and a screen-streaming module. The load-bearing combination is the harvested password plus the tunnel: Expel states the operator can then sign in to internal and external company systems without triggering alerts based on logins from unknown addresses or geolocations. Expel assesses at low-to-medium confidence that the toolkit belongs to a ransomware group or an access broker selling to one.
objects.name: SynkLoader: a Teams message from a lookalike tenant, an MSI called 'PowerShell Cleaner', and a six-module toolkit whose fake lock screen harvests the domain password its own tunnel then uses from the victim's IP

objects.description:
A Joomla events extension's bundled Calendar module can stay vulnerable for three package releases without the extension manager ever showing it

The Joomla CNA published CVE-2026-67365 on 2026-08-14: an unauthenticated SQL injection in mod_icagenda_calendar, the Calendar module bundled with iCagenda, reachable via Joomla's anonymous front-end AJAX entry point with no session, token or account required. Affected 4.0.0–4.0.11; fixed in 4.0.12. The Calendar module's own version stayed pinned at 4.0.7 through three intervening package releases, so a site's extension manager can show a current-looking package version while the actually-vulnerable module component is untouched.

objects.description:
Every site that 'patched' Sourcerer between 17 and 26 August was exploitable the entire time, and its own extension manager said otherwise

CVE-2026-74253 (CVSS 4.0 10.0) in Regular Labs' Sourcerer, the Joomla extension that renders embedded PHP/JS/CSS, has been under active exploitation since roughly 2026-08-19 per the Joomla Security Strike Team, two days after the vendor's first "fix" shipped and seven days before a working one existed. Only 16.0.0 (26 Aug) closes it; the Joomla CNA re-scoped the CVE's affected range in place from 1.0.0-13.1.1 to 1.0.0-15.0.0, meaning sites that updated to 14.0.0, 14.0.1 or 15.0.0 in good faith were exploitable throughout.

Taiwan's Administration for Cyber Security confirmed on 2026-08-13 that attackers combined manual hacking with the open-source OpenClaw AI-agent framework against government agencies. Dream Security's technical reconstruction shows a Hermes Agent + OpenClaw multi-agent stack, coordinated by a Bayesian decision engine, mapping 21 government systems from a single portal over four days, cracking 85 accounts via automated password-variation generation and 100%- accurate CAPTCHA solving, and exfiltrating 2,564+ personnel records before expanding toward Taiwan's nuclear safety agency and 7+ energy companies. Tenable frames it as the anchor incident of a seven-incident, three-actor agentic-AI threat cluster.

objects.description:
A Swiss research lab traces a stealer-log leak into DPRK gambling infrastructure and the fake-IT-worker university pipelines behind it

Kudelski Security, a Swiss research lab, reconstructs connections between North Korean state-linked cybercrime and fake-IT-worker operations via a stealer-log leak. An actor it designates "Bismarck," linked to DPRK-run gambling platforms, reused infrastructure overlapping the FakeCalls Android banking trojan. Separately, a DPRK-affiliated manager's own stolen 2021 credential vault held access to historical Emotet loader infrastructure. The investigation names university-affiliated IT-worker pipelines directly relevant to HR/identity-vetting teams screening remote-hire candidates.

objects.description:
An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal

Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 18 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws score CVSS 8.0 each, and CISA's advisory adds two low-severity unauthenticated flaws. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.
objects.name: Claroty Team82: 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory refrigeration controllers chain to unauthenticated root RCE; a deterministic admin password derived from the device's own MAC address is one of THREE independent pre-auth paths

Claroty's own internet-wide scan found thousands of exposed devices.

objects.description:
A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches

PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain, CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4), that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. Fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 (10 September 2026) replace the emergency patches and are the vendor's recommended build (the September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now names 24.1.11 for v24); servers still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2 need to upgrade now. There is no fix for v23 and earlier, and Huntress estimated on 28 August that 47% of the PaperCut installs it tracks ran v23 or older. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10. Hunt.io's recovery of the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) adds a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API, usable when its address allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, and live pivots into 45 victims, with Switzerland among the countries listed.

objects.content: The quotation attributed to the Department of Justice was not what the release says. It was published as "Among the victims of QTFY computer intrusion activity are..."; the release reads "Among the targets of QTFY are...", and the phrase "computer intrusion activity" appears nowhere on the page. Naming an organisation a target of a platform is a weaker claim than naming it a confirmed intrusion victim, so the quotation, the sentence introducing it and the title have all been moved to what DOJ actually states. The title also no longer reads as though the 2018 dating attaches to that list: DOJ gives that date for QTFY activity generally, in the sentence announcing the FBI/NSA advisory.

This entry stated that CVE-2026-21718 is the deterministic admin-password flaw. Claroty does not say that. Its per-CVE table text for that identifier is generic ("an authentication bypass vulnerability... enabling any attackers to bypass the authentication requirement and achieve pre-authenticated code execution", CVSS v3 10.0), and the narrative section that describes the MAC-address-and-date key derivation names no CVE id at all. The binding was an inference by elimination rather than a stated attribution, and a defender tracing the identifier to a patch note would have been misled. The mechanism description stands as reported; the id binding is removed from the title-adjacent claim, the CVE record's affected text, the body and the action, and the sourcing note now states what Claroty does and does not attribute.

This entry said Kudelski's report treats Bismarck as distinct from the already-tracked PurpleDelta IT-worker cluster rather than as an alias. Kudelski's report never mentions PurpleDelta at all, so it makes no such judgement in either direction, and presenting a silence as a stated analytic position is a claim the source does not support. Replaced with what the report does and does not say.

objects.description:
Three unrelated AI platforms, three intrusions, one pattern: gateways and orchestrators concentrate the credentials and execution privilege attackers want

Microsoft Threat Intelligence confirms three separate real-world intrusions against exposed AI infrastructure: a LiteLLM gateway compromised via CVE-2026-42271 chained with CVE-2026-48710, a RAGFlow deployment reached through an unattributed code-execution path, and a Kestra workflow environment exploited via CVE-2026-49869. Credential harvesting and durable persistence recurred across all three despite different initial-access paths; compute monetisation followed in the LiteLLM and Kestra intrusions but not RAGFlow's, whose objective was narrower credential interception. Together they establish AI gateways, retrieval platforms and orchestration services as a distinct, high-value attack surface.

Bern's cantonal cybersecurity law is in force: 24h/72h incident reporting and a named accountable officer per agency

Canton Bern's government council confirmed on 2026-09-10 that its new Gesetz über Informations- und Cybersicherheit (ICSG) and implementing ordinance (IDSV) enter into force on 1 November 2026. Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76461 (CVSS 9.8) on 2026-09-14: an unauthenticated attacker who sends a single crafted email containing SQL statements to a Cisco Secure Email Gateway can execute arbitrary OS commands as root. Cisco confirms active exploitation and says the flaw was found during the resolution of a TAC support case; there is no workaround. Cisco simultaneously shipped a hardening release fixing five further internally-found vulnerabilities in the same product; Cisco's hardening advisory says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be exploited, this one and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519. On 2026-10-31 Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix in light of new information related to exploit code available online, so a 15.5 appliance patched earlier needs a check of its Retro Remediation Engine version. Public Metasploit modules now exist for the exploited injection (merged 2026-11-05, its author's medium-confidence match to CVE-2026-76461) and for a second S/MIME injection that its author believes is CVE-2026-76443, for which Cisco names no fixed 16.0 build.

objects.description:
SentinelLabs: the same DPRK backdoors from a $292M crypto theft resurface on a victim with no crypto ties, in a campaign that uses poisoned Terraform lockfiles

SentinelLabs found the FLATROOF and ROOFDECK macOS backdoors, first documented in April 2026's USD 292 million LayerZero/KelpDAO cryptocurrency theft, on an unrelated victim: a small India-based IT-services provider with no cryptocurrency ties. The campaign's fake job-interview GitHub repositories carry weaponized Terraform provider lockfiles that redirect `terraform init` to attacker-controlled provider registries, though SentinelLabs cannot prove how this victim's backdoors were delivered. Zscaler ThreatLabz independently reports a July 2026 trojanized Terraform provider binary that runs malicious code as soon as Terraform loads it and delivers FLATROOF on macOS, Linux and Windows, which drops ROOFDECK (Windows and macOS variants identified), in a campaign it suspects is TraderTraitor. In the sample SentinelLabs analysed, the second-stage backdoor reads an operator profile's public "website" field on the Nostr decentralized relay network as its command-and-control URL; Zscaler's variants first try a local configuration and an RSA-signed Pastebin dead drop, and use Nostr profile metadata only as a fallback that locates the current Pastebin URL.

objects.description:
Two exploited NetScaler zero-days: one in default configuration, one on by default on VPN servers; no workaround

Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.

Gambit's further 100-plus infected sites, the admin-pod injection route and the hand-picked victims follow its wording, and the Unit 42 safety-control route is stated as its model choice. The headline keeps Gambit's "almost".

Priority recalibrated from high to notable: a DPRK developer-targeting campaign aimed at crypto firms, not Swiss public bodies. A defanged hostname of the public Nostr relay-status service in the text is replaced by a description of the service. The sourcing note is rewritten as plain provenance. The title, headline and summary no longer present the weaponized Terraform lockfile as this victim's delivery method: SentinelLabs cannot prove how the backdoors arrived, which were on disk weeks before the victim cloned a lure repository. An evidence quote is trimmed to drop a relay-service hostname. A claim that the third-stage implant went silent is narrowed to SentinelLabs' last observed beacon, and attacker-chosen lure repository names are removed.

The takeaway said no CVE or Oracle advisory was involved, although ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer it used the WAF bypass for CVE-2026-35273 against FBI Jobs. That link is now attributed to the group, the CVE is recorded with a link to the PeopleSoft campaign entry that carries the patch and hunt actions, the watch-for-an-advisory action is removed, and the priority moves from high to notable because the defender value lies in the already-covered CVE. The FBI's 2026-09-23 statement leaves the point of breach undetermined, and sources differ on whether it confirms the compromise: Krebs on Security reads it as confirmation, while CyberScoop reports no confirmed scope or attribution. The group's motive is now given in its own words, including its later description of the confrontation as a marketing campaign. Figures and the analyst-role detail are cited to the outlets that carry them, the takeaways are folded into one, and the arrested suspect is no longer named.

Adds that the LivePatch for this flaw does not fix CVE-2026-93616, a separate pre-authentication flaw in the same management servers that Check Point disclosed on 2026-09-22 as exploited in targeted attacks on July 23, and links that entry. A sentence of editorial narration in the main text is rephrased. The fix now includes the Jumbo Hotfix route, so R81.10 is shown as fixable through Take 192 and only R80.x and R81 as unfixed. An invented benign-lookalike triage discriminator is replaced by Check Point's own hunting checks, the trigger wording is narrowed to what Check Point states, and the sk1000171 advisory is added to the sources. The CVE-2026-93616 product scope and the missing LivePatch now cite Check Point's own advisory, the Triage line names the CVE its core-dump criterion belongs to, the headline no longer states the oversized-username trigger as fact, and an uncited exposure characterization is replaced by Check Point's Trusted Clients mitigation.

The detection guidance carried no citation although it comes from Arista's advisory, which also lists behavioral compromise artifacts the entry omitted. The Detection line now cites Arista and describes the backdoor's persistence behavior and log artifact without indicator values, and the Triage line is tightened to what that guidance supports. The immediate action and takeaway no longer present a switch to PSK Edge authentication as a vendor control, since Arista names none and does not say which certificate modes are exposed, and they now carry Arista's own interim controls. The triage line no longer claims an orchestrator never makes outbound web connections, the artifact description keeps to what Arista lists, and the detection, triage and takeaway lines are separated. The default-config tag is removed, since Arista says only orchestrators with certificate-based Edge authentication configured are exposed.

The CVSS 7.8 figure came from the MITRE CVE record rather than from a cited advisory. It now cites Red Hat's CVE page, which publishes the same 7.8 score, and an evidence quote taken from the MITRE record is removed. The main text and action now carry the sourced interim mitigation (block esp4, esp6 and rxrpc, or disable unprivileged user namespaces) and the sourced patch status and discovery credits. Unsupported module names, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, a kernel version range, wider patch coverage and a leftover table of three unrelated CVEs are removed, as is an unrelated actor link. The 2026-09-05 section now attributes the 7.8 score to Red Hat and cites Aikido for its container and detection guidance, which no longer says a module listing confirms IPsec use.

objects.description:
Fortinet now names fixed FortiMail builds for an unauthenticated file-write flaw it confirmed exploited as a zero-day

Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-175 of 2026-10-01 describes a path traversal in FortiMail that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests, and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Belnet, the Belgian government and research network, says a zero-day in its supplier Fortinet's technology let attackers copy its inbound mail from 2026-07-22 and links this advisory, which puts exploitation about ten weeks before the disclosure. Fortinet's revision of 2026-10-05 names the fixed builds 8.0.2, 7.6.7 and 7.4.9 and tells 7.2 users to move to branch 7.4 or above; the vendor workarounds remain the interim control. Fortinet says it remediated FortiMail Cloud on 2026-10-05, so only self-managed appliances need action.

objects.description:
Zammad 6.5.5 is an emergency fix for the exploited session-leak RCE on 6.5; 7.2.2 fixes the root escalation

DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.

external_references.source_name: DIVD CSIRT (public statements on the hack)

objects.name: CVE-2026-102489 / CVE-2026-102490, Zammad helpdesk: a session-hijack remote code execution and a zammad-to-root escalation, both reported exploited since 21 September; 7.2.2 fixes the root flaw on DEB and RPM installs

objects.description:
A national research and government network had its mail copied for 65 days through a zero-day in Fortinet technology

Belnet, the Belgian research and education network that also serves the Belgian government, says an attacker used a zero-day in technology from its supplier Fortinet to copy all incoming mail to Belnet-owned domains between 2026-07-22 and 2026-09-25, plus every download link its FileSender and FedSender transfer services generated and sent directly. Belnet links Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-175, the FortiMail path traversal, without naming the product; the actor is not named.
objects.name: Belnet, the Belgian government and research network, confirms a supplier zero-day let attackers copy all incoming mail to Belnet-owned domains and the transfer links its FileSender and FedSender services sent directly for 65 days

The earlier bulletin APSB26-134 (build 9401, 2026-08-25) fixed three more unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws. On 2026-10-27 the Priority 2 bulletin APSB26-162 fixed eight further Critical flaws in build 9402 and earlier, one needing neither privileges nor user interaction (CVE-2026-105781, SQL injection, 9.8), so build 9403 is now the fix. objects.description:
Symantec: Warlock's operator steals SharePoint machine keys, forges signed payloads and ships ransomware via SYSVOL

Symantec reports that Longlegs (also known as Storm-2603), the China-nexus developer of Warlock ransomware, attacked at least four organizations in two months, a water utility, a telecommunications provider, a regional government body and a university in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries, and still gets in through on-premises SharePoint Server. In the intrusion Symantec walks through, a web shell harvested the farm's ASP.NET machine keys to forge signed payloads, a security-tool killer ran on at least 40 hosts in about two hours, and Warlock reached at least 33 hosts through SYSVOL replication.

objects.description:

The command installs an MSI that starts a signed Canon application sideloading a malicious DLL, which unpacks a RAT with remote desktop, camera and microphone capture and DNS-over-HTTPS command resolution; Huntress has responded to at least 40 incidents from the Google Sites domain, two confirmed through a Custom GPT.

After one server went back into production prematurely, the actor returned with the same account and planted a credential-harvesting script in the login page's jQuery file. objects.content: The headline says Citrix has published no workaround. objects.description: Danish authorities disclosed on 2026-10-05 that unauthorised parties abused a private Danish company's lawful search access to the Central Person Register (CPR) and obtained names, addresses and CPR numbers of about 8.8 million registered persons; Datatilsynet describes a very large number of automated lookups to identify valid CPR numbers. The company is Pays ApS of Odense, which confirmed it to TV 2; Politiken reports that at least three of its accounts, including the administrator account, used the password 123456, and Ritzau puts the access at 21 days and 17 hours from 10 September, where the minister had said about ten days; an anonymous hacker says the access began with a leaked former employee's password, which is the hacker's claim (Danish Ministry of Research, Education and Digitalisation, 2026-10-05; Datatilsynet, 2026-10-05; The Copenhagen Post (Ritzau), 2026-10-10; TV4 Nyheterna (TT), 2026-10-08).

objects.description:
Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record, rejected on 16 October, was restored on 19 October; the exploited flaw stands

Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, without saying what the evidence is. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application. The record for this ID was marked rejected on 2026-10-16 with only a generic reason and ENISA's database shows it restored with its full description on 2026-10-19, while Atlassian's advisory and fixed versions read unchanged, so tooling keyed on the ID may have dropped the flaw in between.

The company, Pays ApS of Odense, confirmed to TV 2 that its lawful access was abused, and Politiken reports that at least three of its accounts, including the administrator account, used the password 123456; Ritzau puts the access at 21 days and 17 hours from 10 September, where the minister had described about ten days. An anonymous hacker told Politiken the access began with a leaked former employee's password, which is the hacker's claim, and Datatilsynet describes a very large number of automated lookups made to identify valid CPR numbers.

objects.description:
Exploited WordPress plugin XSS ends in a hidden admin and persistence that patching does not remove

Patchstack reports that since 2026-10-04 one campaign has been exploiting two unrelated stored cross-site scripting flaws, CVE-2026-93836 in WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to 8.6.6 and CVE-2026-94504 in Ninja Forms up to 3.15.3, by planting a script in an order or a form submission that runs when a logged-in administrator opens it. objects.description: CloudSEK: Azazel is an affiliate that used the Gentlemen's tooling and ransom-note template but kept the proceeds

CloudSEK: a Gentlemen affiliate reached victims through stolen GitLab CI/CD secrets and drove attacks over MCP

CloudSEK analysed two exposed servers of "Azazel", a Russian-speaking affiliate of the Gentlemen ransomware group who also ran his own leak site, and reports about 6 TB of stolen data from some two dozen organisations, among them government-adjacent infrastructure. It says every victim outside one AI-platform intrusion was reached through stolen CI/CD secrets, mainly GitLab variable stores and git history, and that the deeper intrusion into an AI platform chained server-side request forgery, a recovered master key that decrypted the configuration and a token recovered from git history, and that Azazel drove attack commands through an MCP server on a local port. The report is a single source and names no victim.

Unit 42 describes a March 2026 campaign by an Iranian-nexus cluster it calls CL-STA-1178 against an individual in Iraqi critical infrastructure, in which a recruiter persona impersonating Dubai Airports IT sent a coding-test Visual Studio project whose project file runs code during the design-time build, before any compile. Huntress describes a phishing campaign seen since 2026-09-10 in which an Outlook email links to a fake reference document on a legitimate Power BI domain; a "Download Reference" button opens an attacker page that fingerprints the visitor and then downloads a ScreenConnect installer. The installer deploys a rogue ScreenConnect client that establishes a second one, and in one incident a PowerShell script removed the first; Huntress could not obtain the original email, and the configuration of one of the rogue clients also appeared on 22 other endpoints.

objects.description:
A Defender bypass that needs no vulnerability: fill the disk during every update and the engine stays up, stale

LevelBlue SpiderLabs reproduced BigDiskBuster, a proof of concept published on GitHub on 2026-09-19 by the actor known as MSNightmare, which watches the C: volume for Defender update activity and claims the free space so each update fails while the Defender service keeps running and real-time protection stays on. It runs from a standard account and has no CVE or patch; Microsoft says Defender Antivirus detects the proof of concept, and no use in attacks is reported.

objects.description: Tamedia (relayed by Inside IT, 2026-10-20): the involved federal bodies assume Akira is responsible; neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed it

PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB

PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack; the demand rests on the press reports. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich has suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's system, PK Softech cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira.

The FBI, CISA, NSA, NCSC UK and partners from five more countries published AA26-281A on 2026-10-08 on China-linked actors enabled by Integrity Technology Group, whose tactics the advisory calls consistent with Flax Typhoon: open-source and MicroScan vulnerability scanning, XSS credential harvesting, password spraying against Exchange and Microsoft 365 interfaces, SoftEther VPN persistence, DCSync and bulk mail theft through Exchange Web Services. objects.description:
Talos: malware tells the analysing LLM to skip it; the text is plain and therefore detectable

Cisco Talos documents 84 samples from four malware families, collected from January 2025 to July 2026, that embed plain natural-language text meant to steer the LLM stage of automated triage: a verbatim "no need to analyze this file" comment reused by at least four actors, templated variants, instructions repeated across seven chat-template formats, and intimidation or fabricated-authority text. ESET separately found UAC-0099 using a decoy request in a script comment to trip an LLM scanner's refusal; Talos' own test of five local models put the best techniques at steering the outcome in the attacker's favour in about 35% of runs, and its advice is to treat text inside a sample as evidence, never as instruction.
objects.name: Cisco Talos: malware now embeds natural-language instructions aimed at LLM triage pipelines, from a copied comment to template-sprayed prompts across four families, and a Russia-aligned group uses it too

objects.description:
ReliaQuest: AI agents took a Tomcat server to SYSTEM in under a day through an exposed job-submission feature

ReliaQuest assesses with high confidence that LLM-driven agents carried out substantial parts of an intrusion it investigated, using only known techniques: an internet-facing Apache Tomcat application accepted Spring Batch job definitions without a login, jobs ran JavaScript through the Nashorn engine inside the application process, plaintext SQL Server sysadmin credentials from the application's configuration led to xp_cmdshell, and two public privilege-escalation tools reached SYSTEM. ReliaQuest names no victim, sector or region, nor the vendor of the exposed application, and could not determine how many agents ran, which model drove them or how much a person approved.
objects.name: ReliaQuest: LLM-driven agents run most of an intrusion through one unauthenticated Spring Batch job-submission feature on Apache Tomcat, from in-process JavaScript to SYSTEM in under 24 hours

MikroTik's long-term changelogs already carry the fix for a pre-auth RouterOS RCE; its notice still says pending

MikroTik's notice of 2026-10-06 describes CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request body handling of the RouterOS web management service (WebFig, on the www and www-ssl ports) that one crafted request sent without logging in can use to crash the service or run code on the router with full privileges; CISA scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. RouterOS before 7.24, v6 included, is affected where an attacker can reach the web interface; 7.24 fixes the v7 stable channel and MikroTik's changelogs list the fix in 7.23.8 (v7 long-term, 2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term, 2026-10-07), although its notice still shows both long-term releases as pending; MikroTik says the default firewall already blocks the web interface from the internet, and CISA records no known public exploitation.
objects.name: CVE-2026-84411, MikroTik RouterOS: one unauthenticated request to the web management service can run code as root; fixed in 7.24 (v7 stable), 7.23.8 (v7 long-term) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term) (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

objects.description:
Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited

Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.
objects.name: CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134, AhsayCBS backup management console: an unauthenticated authentication-bypass and code-execution chain exploited since 7 October to drop webshells and a cryptominer; Ahsay says its earlier patches were incomplete and ships hotfixes 10.3.4.45 and 9.15.2.70 through its partner portal

objects.description: GitGuardian says the injected-workflow technique GhostAction used was later reused in the Shai-Hulud campaigns and remains at the core of the Mini Shai-Hulud malware family; a technique-reuse statement, not an attribution

GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough

StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. GitGuardian's own data puts the wave of 8 to 12 October at more than 30,000 repositories reached through about 1,900 compromised GitHub accounts, and says GitHub has prevented the workflow from running since 9 October. Between 13 and 21 October the operator pushed at least 72,026 further commits, mostly from accounts whose tokens were already used on 8 October, including a stealer disguised as a font file that a hidden VS Code task runs on developer machines, outside GitHub's workflow hold, and a cron job that survives cleaning the repository.
objects.name: GhostAction returns: stolen maintainer credentials push a fake security-audit workflow into the victims' own GitHub repositories, which now harvests credentials from the entire git history

objects.description: Attackers compromised the .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone) and .as (American Samoa) country-code registries, changed authoritative DNS records and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google and YouTube names and for other organizations' domains; Chrome blocked them and Google had the issuing authorities revoke the Google certificates; Google names no attacker or entry vector and says it cannot guarantee it found every affected domain (Google Chrome Secure Web and Networking Team, 2026-10-06; The Hacker News, 2026-10-08).
objects.name: ccTLD registry hijacks of .gh, .sl and .as (September 2026)

objects.description: Ransomware attack from about 3:40 a.m. on 2026-10-07 that stopped four zones of the SoftBank Group subsidiary IDC Frontier's IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1 for 495 companies and local governments, with the provider saying customer data in those zones can be restored only from customers' own backups and suspending customer consoles in every region; the intrusion route and the actor are not public (IDC Frontier, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-08; Jiji Press, 2026-10-07).
objects.name: IDC Frontier IDCF Cloud ransomware attack (October 2026)

objects.description: Microsoft's designator for the activity behind the DAEMON Tools supply-chain compromise and at least one operator of NeedyMantis; Microsoft assesses the activity originates from China but has not attributed it to a Chinese nation-state actor (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-09-28).
objects.name: Storm-3069

objects.description: Modular post-compromise malware framework, used since at least October 2025 in targeted intrusions at telecommunications organizations, universities, medical nonprofits, intergovernmental organizations and government contractors; DLL-sideloaded beside legitimate software, unpacked from custom encrypted archives, and extended through modules over a WebSocket C2 channel (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-09-28).
objects.name: NeedyMantis

objects.description: Linux botnet malware tracked by Lumen's Black Lotus Labs since April 2026 (campaign name Canto Incognito) that derives its command-and-control address from words in a poem in a GitHub repository, deploys XMRig and Iron miners and turns infected servers into scanners and exploit launchers against exposed LiteLLM, Gotenberg, Ollama and Gitea servers; Lumen assesses that the botnet is associated with an Italian-speaking threat actor (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-07).
objects.name: PoeLLM

objects.description:
Registry-level DNS hijacks of .gh, .sl and .as produced valid HTTPS certificates for Google names

Google's Chrome team reported on 2026-10-06 that attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, changed authoritative DNS records and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains and for domains of other organizations; Chrome blocked them and Google had the issuing authorities revoke the Google certificates. Google names no attacker or entry vector and says it cannot guarantee it found every affected domain; The Hacker News found 12 certificates for Google and YouTube names in public logs, 11 issued by Let's Encrypt and one by ZeroSSL, first logged between 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-27.

external_references.source_name: Google Chrome Secure Web and Networking Team

objects.name: Attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, rewrote authoritative DNS and obtained valid HTTPS certificates for Google and YouTube names

objects.description:
Lumen: a botnet takes its C2 address from a GitHub poem and spreads through exposed AI and developer servers

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs tracks PoeLLM, a financially motivated botnet active since at least April 2026 that Lumen says has impacted more than 3,400 servers, mostly in the United States and Western Europe, among them exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers, with Ivanti Sentry possibly targeted. The malware derives its command-and-control address from words in a poem in a GitHub repository, runs XMRig and Iron miners and turns victims into scanners and exploit launchers that Lumen says likely abuse the LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 path.
objects.name: PoeLLM: a cryptomining botnet that reads its C2 address out of a GitHub poem compromises exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers and turns them into scanners

objects.description:
IDCF Cloud ransomware began with an open-source flaw in the customer portal's login system; no server data left

IDC Frontier, a SoftBank Group subsidiary, says a ransomware attack from about 3:40 a.m. on 2026-10-07 stopped four zones of its IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1, affecting 495 companies and local governments. Its seventh report of 2026-10-27, which closes the investigation, says an open-source flaw in the authentication system of the customer portal was exploited, after which the attacker took administrator rights on the virtualisation platform through the management console, stopped customers' virtual servers and encrypted them; it finds no trace of server data leaving, says portal registration data of up to 71 customers was queried and that backups are retrievable for 206 customers. The software is not named.
objects.name: IDC Frontier: ransomware stops four zones of IDCF Cloud for 495 companies and local governments; the provider's seventh report traces it to an open-source flaw in the customer portal's authentication system and says no server data left

objects.content: SonicWall's own advisories named exploitation in both SMA1000 waves, July and September, so the headline's claim that vendor-named exploitation was new this time was wrong. The summary also attributed to SonicWall's advisory the affected and fixed builds for CVE-2026-102255 that The Hacker News reports. The patch action now names the current fixed builds directly, and a conditional action that restated the body is dropped.

The 2026-09-25 record said the operator rebuilt its infrastructure within hours; Computing UK reports only that the attacker repeatedly rebuilt it and continued. The technique mapping gains the timestamp restoration Gambit describes.

CISA's KEV record for CVE-2026-86950 does not set the forensic-triage flag, so the statement that CISA attached its forensic-triage requirements to the listing is withdrawn. The CVE's EPSS value is corrected from 0.81 (a percentage figure read as a probability) to FIRST's 0.01242.

Arctic Wolf's June report describes Impacket-consistent SMB reconnaissance in a subset of intrusions that did not progress beyond session setup, not lateral movement, and its sector list describes the exploitation wave as a whole. Two hunting lines named log fields and Windows event ids no source gives and are rewritten. Added: Rapid7 and Unit 42 saw no post-access activity or lateral movement in the May and early June intrusions, Rapid7 saw the same spoofed client MAC address in both waves, and Rapid7 published a proof of concept the day CISA listed the flaw.

CloudSEK's key finding says every confirmed victim was reached through stolen CI/CD secrets, but its own account of the AI-platform intrusion starts with a server-side request forgery in an image API, and elsewhere it says every victim outside that engagement was reached through CI/CD secrets. The summary now carries the qualified form and the sourcing note states the inconsistency.

The June hunting paragraph named Windows event ids and a domain-wide rotation that no cited source gives; Fortinet's guidance is to treat directory accounts the device used as compromised and review domain controller logs. The October paragraph had attributed a FortiGate audit-log mapping to the FBI and Secret Service advisory, which names only the logs to review. The action keeps the single do-now task.

Elastic reads the commit-message string warning against token revocation as intimidation, and OX Security calls the same string an extortion string while describing a dead man's switch separately, which Elastic does not mention; the containment paragraph now says so. Unit 42's environment check selects a single republishing path in one project and does not gate the worm as a whole, which the earlier wording implied. The locale-gate sentence gains its citation.

The Exposure line gave only S4GET's kernel scope, so a reader on an older kernel line would have concluded neither flaw applied; OVERPASS, the CVSS 10.0 flaw, affects kernel lines from 7.22 to 9.20. The headline no longer calls both flaws maximum severity (S4GET is 9.8), and the ACL sentence gains its citation.

Zscaler describes FLATROOF payloads for macOS, Linux and Windows that drop the ROOFDECK backdoor, and identifies ROOFDECK variants only for Windows and macOS; the summary had said both families were delivered on all three platforms. The macOS detection sentence gains its SentinelLabs citation.

Adds CyberScoop's citation to two sentences it carries (the DiMaggio and Kaiser warnings and DiMaggio's brand assessment) and attributes the FBI's non-confirmation to BleepingComputer's recap of the bureau's first response, which its later statements overtook. A reference to the earlier entry on the shared CVE is added; the two are distinct findings.

NCSC-NL's advisory says Fortinet fixed CVE-2026-25089 in FortiSandbox versions 4.2 through 5.0.5, while Fortinet's advisory table starts at 4.4.0; the entry followed the table without saying the sources differ, so a 4.2 operator could have concluded they were not exposed. The Exposure line and the action now cover 4.2, and the title marks 9.8 as the base score.

The entry was a bare migrated update that never said what Copy Fail is. CISA added the flaw to its catalog on 2026-05-01, not 2026-05-06; the Ubuntu and RHEL kernel versions given were not the vendors' fixed builds; and Microsoft does not describe the two flaws as used complementarily or via SSH credential stuffing, only limited su escalation that may be either. CERT-EU's advisory is dated 2026-04-29, the KEV catalogue landing page is dropped, and the entry is rewritten as a vulnerability entry from Xint's disclosure, CERT-EU, the KEV record and Ubuntu's tracker, with the CVE record, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping, and labelled guidance, including the module blacklist as the interim measure. A reference to the WordPress WP2Shell entry, which also cites this CVE, is added.

Exploitation of Dirty Frag is not confirmed: Microsoft's observation may be Dirty Frag or Copy Fail, and Microsoft does not report exfiltration, so the exploited status is removed. The root cause is in-place decryption of a spliced page-cache page, not DMA remapping; only the ESP variant needs a user namespace; the tested distributions and Ubuntu releases were wrong; Red Hat's bulletin does not cover CVE-2026-43500, which does not affect Red Hat, and its targeted sysctl is user.max_user_namespaces; a file-write watch cannot see the page-cache write; and Microsoft does not mention AIDE, IMA or auditd. The summary's pending-patch state is superseded: both mainline fixes and distribution kernels are released. CVSS for CVE-2026-43284 is the CNA's 8.8, the duplicate Red Hat source and self-quoted evidence are removed, and the earlier sections are corrected in place. The two flaws' write primitives are told apart (4 chosen bytes into a setuid binary for ESP, 8 brute-forced bytes into /etc/passwd for RxRPC), the Copy Fail CVE is cited to Microsoft, the on-disk clause to Aikido, the AFS effect to Ubuntu, the 2013 bug is described without a function name the sources do not give, the NCSC-CH citation points at the public hub post, and the action is cut to the patch task. The main analysis gains Exposure and takeaway lines.

The six GINA v2 flaws were not all fixed in '15.0.4 (patch 15.0.4.1)': CVE-2026-44128 was fixed in 15.0.2.1 and CVE-2026-44126 in 15.0.3, the rest in 15.0.4, and 15.0.4.1 is an unrelated hotfix. SEPPmail is based in Neuenhof, not Steinach, and the customer claims had no source. Four CVEs were mistyped as code execution. CVE-2026-2743 was already fixed in March, not new in May; the vendor and InfoGuard disagree on its fix version; and InfoGuard found it rather than performing an earlier review. The entry is rewritten with per-CVE types and fix versions, a contradiction line, a current-release action, a rating and an ATT&CK mapping. A Detection line follows InfoGuard's CVE-2026-2743 chain, the contradiction line adds the 15.0.3 or 15.0.4 split for CVE-2026-44126, and the 10.0 score for CVE-2026-2743 is cited to The Hacker News. The Detection line places the traversal in the request body InfoGuard shows, and the CVE-2026-44126 record states both fixed-version readings.

The headline victimology was wrong: no EU government victim is reported; EU countries appear only among infection attempts, the backdoor reached about a dozen machines in Russia, Belarus and Thailand, and QUIC RAT one educational institution in Russia. Kaspersky does not describe keylogging, SOCKS proxying or tunnelling for QUIC RAT, does not attribute the attack, and calls the intent unclear; the Linux masquerade and asymmetric-cryptography mappings had no source. The Securelist report becomes the primary source, the espionage and China-nexus tags are removed, and the entry gains a rating and a supported ATT&CK mapping. Priority moves from high to notable. The startup behaviour and the Detection line now lead with the backdoor's beacon to a typosquatted vendor domain, which precedes any cmd.exe execution.

CISA did not issue Emergency Directive 26-03 on 2026-05-14: the directive dates from 2026-02-25, and on 2026-05-14 CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog under it. The NETCONF and SSH-key path Rapid7 demonstrated is on the Controller, not the Manager; Talos names exactly ten other clusters exploiting a separate set of February flaws; the segmentation mitigation had no source; and the flaw is an authentication bypass, not code execution. The entry is rewritten with the Validator added, Cisco's indicators and pre-upgrade evidence step, the UAT-8616 attribution, verbatim evidence, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping and a link to the separate CVE-2026-20245 entry. Rapid7's Metasploit module, submitted to the public framework repository, is now named, and the flaw's status gains poc-public.

The title, summary, body and action still said no patch existed, although fixed releases shipped from 2026-06-09 and Cisco added a Live Protect shield. CVE-2026-20245 was typed as an unauthenticated bypass with no score; it is an authenticated local netadmin-to-root flaw scored 7.8, and the companion CVE-2026-20182 scores 10.0. Mandiant dates the zero-day exploitation to April 2026 at a service provider, not late 2025 to March at a communications provider; it presents the peering-bypass foothold as a possibility, and reports file deletion and configuration rollback rather than history or syslog deletion. The entry is rewritten with the Controller and Validator, the KEV listing, Cisco's and Mandiant's indicators, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping and a link to the CVE-2026-20182 entry; both Mandiant sections are corrected in place and workflow references removed. The companion CVE-2026-20127 record gains Cisco's 10.0 score and its KEV listing, and the attacker's file and account names are replaced with descriptions of the behaviour.

depthfirst found the flaw on 2026-04-18, reported it on 2026-04-21 and shared its proof of concept on 2026-05-05; no source mentions an NDA or a 2026-04-28 PoC handover. The affected-version ranges for the Kubernetes and F5 products had gaps the earlier text closed over, and the NGINX project's own medium severity rating was not set against the 9.2 score. The entry gains the nginx.org advisory, Security Affairs and The Hacker News as sources, VulnCheck's honeypot exploitation attempts carried over from the duplicate entry of 2026-05-18, a contradiction line, exposure and detection lines, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping, the affected products and a link to the SAP August patch-day entry. The exploitation-status sentence now reads as NCSC-CH dated it, ahead of VulnCheck's report, and the score attributions name only what each cited page states.

The summary still said no party reported exploitation, which the entry's own update of 2026-08-16 superseded with Defused's honeypot attempts. The rebuild-and-redeploy requirement for the NGINX-related note comes from Onapsis rather than SAP's patch-day page and now carries that citation, the note is identified as SAP's fix for the upstream NGINX flaw, and the entry links the NGINX entry. The main analysis no longer says no party reports exploitation, and its two statements about where the component sits and where legitimate imports come from are marked as analyst judgement; the NCSC-NL evidence quote is given in English with the Dutch original, and two overlapping Commerce Cloud actions are merged. No cited source calls the vulnerable endpoint an import endpoint, so the title, action and detection lines name the Data Hub Adapter endpoint; the patch-day status follows NCSC-CH's unknown rating, the remaining inferences are marked as analyst judgement, the CVE-2026-58243 sentence gains its citation, and earlier sections no longer refer to the entry itself. CVE-2026-58231 is no longer marked exploited: the reports are Defused's honeypot attempts, which NCSC-NL relays, and no party reports a compromised instance, the same standard the nginx entry applies. Note 3773203 is described in SAP's own words, and the Data Hub Adapter record names the affected releases.

Adds references to the other entries that share CVE-2025-8088 (the Gamaredon tooling consolidation and the Turla StockStay entry), which are distinct findings, an ATT&CK mapping of the delivery and stealing behaviour the body describes, and replaces a self-quoted evidence record with a verbatim Trend Micro sentence. The move off Telegram is attributed to SHADOW-EARTH-066 alone, with the source's own hedge on its cause, and the entry now says Trend Micro is the only analyst of both campaigns, relayed by The Hacker News.
