objects.description: Microsoft assesses that Storm-0940 was responsible; an attribution by Microsoft alone, which ConnectWise has not confirmed

ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access

ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.

objects.content: The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. The headline no longer calls both zero-days default-configuration: CVE-2026-88772 needs DTLS, on by default only on VPN virtual servers. objects.description:
Calendar-invite phishing spreads: Outlook and Gmail add the lure on their own and keep it after the email is deleted

Netcraft reports that phishing lures delivered as ICS calendar files, adopted by widespread campaigns of the EvilTokens Microsoft 365 token-stealing kit, are now spreading to low-effort scams. Outlook with Exchange Online (desktop, web and mobile) and Gmail with Google Calendar add such an invite to the calendar automatically as tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, so purging the message leaves the lure in place. EvilTokens invites posed as meetings, alerts or voicemail and led to a device-code page that has the victim authorise an attacker's device through OAuth; Sublime Security, quoted by The Guardian, reports exponential growth in calendar phishing.
objects.name: Phishing lures sent as ICS calendar invites land in Outlook and Gmail calendars without a click and stay after the email is deleted; EvilTokens used them for Microsoft 365 device-code phishing

objects.description:
OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it

OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, available for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Its postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on the developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched.

objects.description:
BACS grades logins in five classes: static secrets should in principle go; session binding resists phishing

Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) published on 2026-10-19 a technology assessment that sorts authentication methods, tokens and services into the classes tief, mittel and hoch, with a star on mittel and hoch for resistance to real-time phishing. It says methods in class tief, those built on a secret that is the same at every login, should in principle no longer be used. The classification is non-binding and gives no basis for testing or certification; it is a rough guideline from the federal authority for writing authentication requirements.
objects.name: BACS publishes five security classes for authentication methods: static secrets should in principle no longer be used, and only session-bound methods resist real-time phishing

objects.description:
Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6, 1.31.7 and Debian trixie, not bookworm

The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 while its bookworm package is still marked vulnerable.

objects.description:
PHP2Shell: CISA lists both flaws as exploited after honeypot code execution; update the runtime, not the CMS

The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; GreyNoise's sensors have recorded shell sessions since 2026-10-28, Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, Dream Research recovered a custom build chained with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that rooted 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and attacked a US government-affiliated network, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

objects.description:
Joint advisory on SafePay: VPN credentials and five old edge and backup flaws in, backup NAS wiped before encryption

CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service, Germany's LKA Rheinland-Pfalz and UK law enforcement published advisory AA26-293A on 2026-10-20 on SafePay, which they say was among the most active ransomware groups in 2026 and has affected at least 600 victims, in Europe among other regions. Access comes from exposed credentials, brute force and phished account profiles used over Mullvad VPN addresses, and from five known flaws in Cisco ASA and Firepower Threat Defense, Veeam Backup and Replication and SonicWall SonicOS; the distinctive step is stopping the Volume Shadow Copy Service and factory-resetting the network storage that holds backups before encryption.

objects.description:
Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; Windows drops seven certificates, and Java, Python, Go and GitLab need updates

On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them; Microsoft went further on 2026-10-26 and removed seven eMudhra-hierarchy certificates from the Windows trust list, and from the Edge trust list on 2026-10-27. Software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated: Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, GitLab in its releases of 2026-10-29, Python added a built-in denylist as CVE-2026-115557, and Java needs the second update of 2026-10-24 (CVE-2026-114820, CVSS 3.1 9.1) even on a runtime updated in the past few days. Chrome's removal of the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root was due on 2026-10-27; Cisco's advisory dates its ISE fixes to December 2026 and April 2027, and no exploitation is reported.

objects.description: Symantec attributes the HOOKEDGE intrusions to Swallowtail, which it equates with APT28; Recorded Future assesses with moderate confidence that BlueDelta, overlapping APT28, used it

Symantec: APT28's hidden-Edge backdoor hit law-enforcement and defence targets; at a shipbuilder it added an SSH tunnel

Symantec reports that APT28, which it tracks as Swallowtail, used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft-engine manufacturer in two NATO member states, none named. A macro-enabled Word document started a script chain that uses a hidden, off-screen Microsoft Edge window as its HTTP client against a public webhook service; at the shipbuilder the operators then pushed an SSH private key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes from the host itself and ran a previously undocumented in-memory loader, in an intrusion that lasted at least two months. Recorded Future had documented HOOKEDGE against government and diplomatic targets in Romania, Spain and Turkiye in August.

objects.description:
Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them

TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.
objects.name: TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix

objects.content: Police authorities, banks, hospitals, schools and prisons are the firm's customers as AWP describes them, not organisations reported in the stolen data; the organisations reported as concerned are judicial entities including the Établissements de la plaine de l'Orbe, gendarmerie premises, several banks and several dozen companies.

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, not CVE-2026-46300 specifically; the summary and the 2026-09-05 section now attribute it that way, and no source describes a Kubernetes exploit for this CVE. Detection and triage lines are added from Wiz's description of the public exploit and Red Hat's list of legitimate user-namespace uses.

The June dataset figures come from three researchers, and BleepingComputer reports firewall URLs and apparently valid credentials, some confirmed authentic, rather than management URLs and valid credentials: Hudson Rock counted 73,932 URLs in 194 countries and 21,632 domains, Kevin Beaumont put it at about 75,000 devices. SOCRadar's Lynx / INC attribution dates from its 29 June update, while BleepingComputer's October recap dates it to July. The Detection line adds the FBI and Secret Service configuration review, with particular attention to added unrecognized accounts, and the account deletions and password changes they report on compromised devices.

Palo Alto's advisory makes the one-time re-authentication an automatic consequence of the PAN-OS upgrade, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie, not a step to force; the action and the 2026-06-10 and 2026-10-06 sections now say so. The CVE record carries the affected trains and fixed builds from the advisory, and a triage line adds Arctic Wolf's pattern of a cookie decryption failure followed quickly by a successful cookie login.

Code execution was described as possible only with ASLR disabled; depthfirst notes that forked workers share one heap layout that could in theory leak ASLR, and F5's CVE description, updated on 2026-09-10, covers systems where the attacker can bypass ASLR, against NCSC-CH's narrower statement. The headline now names the public proof of concept and VulnCheck's honeypot exploitation attempts, and verbatim quotes from the GitHub advisory, depthfirst, ENISA EUVD and The Hacker News back the trigger, disclosure, ASLR and exploitation statements. A Defender takeaway now names the fixed NGINX Open Source releases and depthfirst's named-capture workaround, replacing the standing action that restated them.

The interim mitigation was given as a module blacklist for every distribution, but Red Hat builds algif_aead into its kernel, where it cannot be blocklisted; Red Hat's boot argument that blocks the affected functions is now given for RHEL, together with Xint's seccomp option and Red Hat's statement that all its fixes are available.

PAN-OS management interfaces were rooted in the wild via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw: hotfix, then check for compromise

Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.

objects.description:
GitLab's critical patch fixes an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 RCE in Org-mode rendering; no exploitation reported

GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-110264 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in regular-expression handling that lets an unauthenticated user run code on a self-managed GitLab server as the git user; GitLab's own detection write-ups place it in the rendering of .org files, which needs only a public project that can hold the payload. Every version from 7.0 before 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1 is affected, so instances on the 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 builds that closed the earlier regular-expression flaws still need this release. The bug sits in Ruby's own regular-expression engine, which Ruby fixed on 2026-10-23 in 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13, so any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to it. GitLab does not report exploitation.

objects.description:
LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it

On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0, the open-source LLM gateway, shipped with malicious Python startup files in all seven PyPI wheels (live 11:39 to 13:23 UTC) and in the official GHCR and Docker Hub images behind the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable tags (11:46 to 14:20 UTC); they run a credential stealer at every Python start and start a background loader that could execute code fetched from an attacker-chosen host, though Socket saw its pointer empty at 13:01 UTC. The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 says a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker, from 2026-10-10, a GitHub organization owner's CLI token, with which it stole two maintainers' tokens and, on 2026-10-21, overrode branch protection to build the release from a look-alike repository; Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running on 2026-10-10. Wiz saw stolen AWS instance-role credentials tested about 4.5 hours after exfiltration; PyPI and the registries removed the release the same day and the maintainers say to pin 1.106.2 or an explicit earlier version.

Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs ARTEX at machine speed; Mandiant now sees agent frameworks in incident-response cases

Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns.

objects.description:
Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights

Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date.
objects.name: CVE-2026-114625, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem: an SQL injection lets any authenticated user, down to the Enterprise Read Only role, act as a superuser operator, and Arista says it is actively exploited (CVSS 3.1 9.9)

objects.description:
HPE's Aruba wireless bulletin fixes 19 unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0+; HPE knows of no public exploit code

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 of 2026-10-22 fixes 72 CVEs in AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and access points, 33 of them at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher and 19 of those reachable over the network without authentication (eight at 10.0). HPE found the flaws through internal research, knows of no public discussion or exploit code, and strongly urges patching; its only workaround is to confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated segment behind firewall policy.
objects.name: HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 72 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points

objects.description:
NetScaler's PHP2Shell fix is out: 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and FIPS builds; restrict management access until installed

NetScaler Product Security says the two PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the NetScaler Management Portal, reached through the NSIP GUI, any SNIP that permits management access and the cluster IP GUI, on all supported software versions; NetScaler Console and SVM are not affected. Citrix's bulletin now names the fixed builds, 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS and 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 and later, and tells customers to immediately restrict management access to trusted networks; no source reports an attack on NetScaler, although CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version; fixed in 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and the FIPS and NDcPP builds

objects.description:
Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November

Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited.
objects.name: Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: critical and high-severity fixes in FortiOS 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 and 7.2.14, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with the advisories withheld until 2026-11-10

objects.description:
Huntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed within minutes; a password reset leaves planted devices and MFA methods

Huntress reports that between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 it detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events in 79 organizations that replayed tokens stolen through adversary-in-the-middle relays, device-code phishing and social engineering, within minutes of capture and from one rented hosting range. The operators then registered rogue Entra devices, wiped and replaced MFA methods in 19 organizations and hid mail with inbox rules; a password reset alone removes none of it.
objects.name: M365 token spray and replay: Huntress tracks a 10-week campaign that replays stolen post-MFA tokens from rented hosting within minutes, registers rogue Entra devices, wipes and re-registers MFA methods and hides mail with inbox rules of one to three characters or punctuation only

objects.description: Kaspersky GReAT attributes the BlackX campaign to APT41 with medium confidence (curated relation type: attributed-to)

Kaspersky: a UEFI bootkit ran on fully patched Windows because Microsoft's Secure Boot revocation is off by default

Kaspersky GReAT reports BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus that exploits Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker keys and load a kernel driver that blinds security products, installed after attackers held administrator rights on networks of diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan; Kaspersky attributes it to APT41 with medium confidence. The targeted machines were fully patched, because Microsoft's fix revokes the old boot-manager certificate only when an administrator sets a registry flag and runs a scheduled task.
objects.name: BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it

objects.description:
ESET: a backdoor reaches its C2 through the Yggdrasil mesh; Sandworm wiped the victim two months after UAC-0099 got in

ESET reports that UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company on 2025-07-16 with a spearphishing attachment and a day later deployed MythicRatatoskr, a Go backdoor whose command server sits inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, reached through public peers; on 2025-09-17 the SDelete utility was deployed through Group Policy, which ESET assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access. ESET names blocking the public peer addresses as a viable mitigation.
objects.name: MythicRatatoskr: ESET documents a Go backdoor that hides its command server inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, and a UAC-0099 to Sandworm access handoff that ended in a Group Policy wiper attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics firm

objects.description:
FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed

Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected.
objects.name: Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

objects.description:
Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now

CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app to be disabled.

objects.description:

Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks.

Talos: UAT-11473 implants KeyDrift in Cisco SD-WAN controllers through CVE-2026-20127 to collect data-plane keys

Cisco Talos reports that a cluster it calls UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the peering authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator (CVSS 10.0, fixed releases since February 2026, no workaround), and then ran the KeyDrift implant inside the controller's control-plane process to collect session metadata and what Talos assesses to be data-plane IPsec keys. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says it is aware of limited exploitation, and Talos assesses with high confidence that the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network.
objects.name: KeyDrift: Talos reports UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to run an implant inside the control-plane daemon that collects data-plane keys, with infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network

objects.description:
Veeam fixes an unauthenticated 9.1 authorization bypass on 13.x servers, a VB365 SQL injection and a ONE MFA bypass

Veeam's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix CVE-2026-108142, an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 and 13.0 on Windows and of the Veeam Software Appliance (CVSS 4.0 9.1, fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3; 12.x is not affected), a SQL injection in Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 that reaches code execution as the PostgreSQL service account (9.0, fixed in 8.6) and an MFA bypass in Veeam ONE 13.1 for an attacker holding Administrator credentials (8.5). NCSC Switzerland relayed the Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE advisories on 2026-10-28 and says the vendor reports no evidence of exploitation.
objects.name: CVE-2026-108142, Veeam Backup & Replication: an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of 13.x backup servers (CVSS 4.0 9.1), fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3, with a Backup for Microsoft 365 SQL injection to code execution and a Veeam ONE MFA bypass fixed the same day

objects.description:
WatchGuard fixes three feature-dependent unauthenticated flaws scored 9.2 in Fireware OS; no exploitation known

WatchGuard's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix 17 flaws in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22, seven of them scored 9.0 or higher. Three need no authentication but a specific feature: a heap write in the Access Portal's WebSocket handling, a stack overflow in the SIP proxy and missing authentication in the FireCluster sync daemon, each scored 9.2. Four more need an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to an Active Directory server, to WatchGuard Cloud or to a log server. WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation of any of them.
objects.name: WatchGuard Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and 12.5.22: seven of 17 fixed Fireware OS flaws are scored 9.0 or higher, among them unauthenticated memory-corruption and missing-authentication rows in the Access Portal, the SIP proxy and the FireCluster sync daemon; WatchGuard knows of no exploitation

objects.description:
Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.
objects.name: Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

objects.description: Leak-site self-claim only: Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that Rhysida listed the municipality's file servers, and the municipality has not confirmed the group or the listing

Machelen municipality: foothold from a website's misleading instructions, 22 days to detection; Rhysida lists its files

The Belgian municipality of Machelen published a timeline in which attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, reached a user with high privileges on 2026-09-10 and were found on 2026-09-11; it confirms that personal data was stolen. Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that the Rhysida group had listed the municipal and social-welfare file servers on its leak site, a claim the municipality has not confirmed.

objects.description:
Huntress: phished MDM enrolments push ScreenConnect back after removal; the RMM is not the root of the intrusion

Huntress reports several recent incidents in which phishing victims ended up with an MDM client from Hexnode or Rippling followed by an unauthorised ScreenConnect agent. In the Rippling case the attacker used the MDM, running with SYSTEM rights, to stage and run ScreenConnect; in the Hexnode case the managed-service provider removed ScreenConnect and it returned several hours later to the same relay while the Hexnode client was still installed. Huntress says the products are not at fault and that removing the RMM does not remove the management architecture behind it.
objects.name: Huntress: phished MDM enrolments in Hexnode and Rippling give attackers a management path that brings ScreenConnect back after it has been removed

objects.description:
ESET: an emailed RAR ran code on MDaemon servers via ClamAV's UnRAR; fixed in MDaemon 26.0.4, ClamAV 1.4.6 and 1.5.4

ESET reports an active campaign in Ukraine in which Russia-aligned attackers exploited MDaemon mail servers: a crafted RAR archive mailed to any address makes MDaemon invoke ClamAV, whose old bundled UnRAR library carries the path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088, and the exploit writes a malicious DLL to the server with no user interaction. MDaemon fixed it in 26.0.4 on 2026-08-25, and ClamAV's own notes show that every Windows ClamAV from 0.101.0 to 1.5.3 is affected, fixed in 1.4.6 and 1.5.4. The attackers deployed the HELLAGE mail-stealing backdoor and the Telegram-controlled HELLTAG backdoor.

external_references.source_name: ESET Research (APT Activity Report, April to September 2026)

objects.name: MDaemon mail server below 26.0.4 and Windows ClamAV 0.101.0 to 1.5.3: a crafted RAR emailed to any address runs code on the server through the bundled UnRAR flaw CVE-2025-8088, and ESET saw Russia-aligned attackers use it in Ukraine to deploy the HELLAGE and HELLTAG backdoors

objects.description: SafeDep observes that the worm adds the token-revocation wiper of Mini Shai-Hulud; the lineage is not confirmed (curated relation type: overlaps-with)

SafeDep finds the worm shares code with the June Miasma worm and has not confirmed the lineage; JFrog says its evidence does not establish that the original operators are responsible (curated relation type: overlaps-with)

SafeDep and JFrog: the testmetest npm worm now runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not stop it; 42 repos armed

SafeDep and JFrog describe an npm worm, tracked as testmetest, whose newest builds start when an application imports the package, so installing with --ignore-scripts does not stop it. It steals SSH, registry, cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials, publishes new patch versions of the victim's own packages, and wipes the home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked. SafeDep counts 19 packages from one operator between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-27; JFrog found 42 armed GitHub repositories of 11 legitimate owners; neither lab names an actor.
objects.name: testmetest: an npm worm in the Miasma and Shai-Hulud family now starts when an application imports the package, so install with --ignore-scripts no longer protects, and JFrog finds 42 third-party GitHub repositories already armed with its publisher

objects.description:
Check Point: PHP2Shell hits gateway VPN and portal web interfaces; hotfixes out, R81.20 package reissued 28 October

Check Point's advisory sk1000302, last modified 2026-10-29, says the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2 each) can give remote code execution through the web interfaces of Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls that use Mobile Access, SSL Network Extender VPN, SAML-realm VPN authentication, the Identity Awareness captive portal, the UserCheck portal or Zero Phishing. Hotfixes exist for R81.20, R82, R82.10 and R82.20 and for Spark R82.00 and R81.10; the R81.20 package was reissued on 2026-10-28 for gateways that use Mobile Access, and a hotfix for the end-of-support gateway release R81.10 followed on 2026-10-29. The sk makes no statement on exploitation of Check Point products, and CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Check Point Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the web interfaces of gateways that run Mobile Access, SSL Network Extender, SAML-realm VPN, the Identity Awareness captive portal, UserCheck or Zero Phishing; hotfixes since 2026-10-23, the R81.20 package reissued on 2026-10-28 (CVSS 9.2)

objects.description:
F5 BIG-IP is affected by PHP2Shell: fixes are in 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4; APM data plane and TMUI exposed

F5's release notes for BIG-IP 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4, each updated on 2026-10-24, list K000163821 as the fix for the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and call each a critical release whose only new changes are PHP fixes. NCSC-NL's record of K000163821 puts BIG-IP 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0 in scope, through the Configuration utility of all modules and through the access-profile data plane of APM and SSL Orchestrator; F5's article itself could not be read, and nothing found reports an attack on BIG-IP, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, F5 BIG-IP: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the Configuration utility of every module and the APM and SSL Orchestrator access profiles on 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0, and F5's cumulative critical releases 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4 carry the fix

objects.description:
PHP2Shell: Trend Micro Apex Central and Apex One await patches to 11 Nov; Quest KACE and NetApp ONTAP have fixes

Trend Micro's advisory, last updated 2026-11-02, lists Apex Central and the on-premises Apex One server as impacted by the PHP flaws with critical patches due on 2026-11-11 and interim mitigations, shows critical patches for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector, and adds Mobile Security for Enterprise as impacted with a patch due on 2026-11-17; Quest says all KACE SMA and SDA versions are affected, with SMA 15.0 CU5 and 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix out and advice to block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until applied; and NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, with attacker access as the www user restricted to the PHP jail and hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4. NetApp says it is aware of public discussion of the vulnerability and none of the three vendors reports an exploited case in what was read, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited.

Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround

Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch.

objects.description:
CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4

WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating.
objects.name: WordPress core 4.7 to 7.1.3: an unauthenticated race in the core update process can lead to remote code execution, fixed in 7.1.4 and backported to every supported branch, listed by CISA as exploited; Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977

objects.description:
Talos IR Q3: public administration tied for most targeted; vishing into RMM and EDR killing mark the ransomware cases

Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 trends report names public administration, tied with finance at 18 percent of engagements, as the most targeted sector, and puts phishing first and public-facing application exploitation second among initial-access techniques. Its ransomware cases (27 percent of engagements) show help-desk vishing that leads the victim to allow remote access through a legitimate remote-management tool, and operators who uninstall or terminate EDR, including with vulnerable drivers.
objects.name: ANNUAL REPORT: Cisco Talos Incident Response trends Q3 2026: public administration tied with finance as the most targeted sector, help-desk vishing into remote-management tools, and ransomware operators uninstalling and killing EDR

CrowdStrike: VAPOR PANDA runs ARTEX against 200+ organisations, European foreign ministries among them

CrowdStrike reports that from 2026-10-17 the China-nexus actor VAPOR PANDA used the ARTEX agent framework, driven mainly by the DeepSeek model, against more than 200 organisations worldwide, with the controller CrowdStrike saw directing exploitation in at least 14 countries, including foreign ministries in Europe, a European country's presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and a Greek government entity. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations, with the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor loaded by a renamed legitimate binary, and says this campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported.
objects.name: VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor

objects.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes Silent Train as Volt Typhoon's covert access network

Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim.

objects.description:
Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor

Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name.

objects.description:

Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination.

The analysis no longer says there is no exploitation signal or that the cookie name is withheld; the October 2025 release is treated as a lower bound on exposure, not its start; the CVE record's 9.4 score beside the discloser's 10.0, Membership Pro's CVSS 3.1 rating and its default-configuration impact, Balbooa's wording on web-server rules and the attribution of the read-side reading are corrected; the headline is current.

Dream's report, as updated on 2026-10-29, names the rooted firewalls as PAN-OS, so the 2026-10-29 section now does too and gives Dream's account of what the Active Directory attacks confirmed; the Exposure and takeaway lines now name PAN-OS management interfaces and Palo Alto's fixes. The CISA catalog statement is given in CISA's words, the root-step sentence follows Wiz's wording, and two at-disclosure sentences (Microsoft's no-exploitation statement, which the KEV listing superseded, and the early patch note) are removed.

Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 3.1 8.1) to the WordPress upgrade-window race after the entry was written; the statements that no CVE identifier exists are replaced and the CVE record is added.

An earlier section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside the laboratory is dated to the day it held; NCSC Switzerland now rates the flaw actively exploited, and Zscaler's first-day decoy telemetry joins ELLIO's. Datadog's detection layers (decoder errors, worker crashes, leaked decompressed output) and what does not catch the attack are added, as is Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud Transporter Client.

The fixed versions given for CVE-2026-114148 named runtime releases 10.0.14 and 11.0.0-rc.3; Microsoft's advisory fixes the ASP.NET Core tarballs in 8.0.33 and 9.0.22 and the source-built distributions in SDK releases 8.0.133, 9.0.123, 10.0.114, 10.0.403 and 11.0.100-rc.3. The process-crash signal in the Detection line now rests on JFrog's .NET reproduction.

Broadcom's revisions of 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-19 (the 8.0 U2f express patches and the 7.0 extended-support path) are now in the fixed builds and actions; the Infosecurity Magazine attribution and date are corrected, CISA's ransomware-use flag on CVE-2026-59310 is recorded, the network attack vector of the two lower-severity flaws and the researcher credit are fixed, and the headline is current.

objects.description:
cPGuard update channel pushed a fake root update to about 2,950 servers on 2 Nov; update, then rotate root secrets

OPSSHIELD's disclosure of 2026-11-03 says an attacker registered as a customer on its billing portal and ran commands on the billing and licensing server, through crafted requests to the portal's callback pages (the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access), took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake cPGuard update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02 (02:08 to 03:20 UTC). Sekoia's own assessment with moderate to high confidence, resting partly on unpublished partner and Google TAG inputs
Sekoia names AndroSnitch as the payload of the Android chain

APT29-linked watering hole uses n-day iOS and Chrome chains; CISA lists CVE-2024-27834; updated devices resist

Sekoia reports a watering-hole campaign it assesses with moderate to high confidence to be APT29 or a subgroup, serving platform-specific exploit chains for iOS 16.7, a DarkSword-based iOS chain and Chrome 139 to 145 on Android through injected sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy analytics script; Sekoia says none of the chains works against fully updated devices. CISA added the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834, the second step of the iOS 16.7 chain and fixed in May 2024, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-04; no Swiss victim is named.
objects.name: Sekoia: an APT29-linked watering hole serves n-day iOS and Android exploit chains through compromised sites, clone domains and a one-week compromise of the Plerdy tracker; CISA lists the Apple WebKit pointer-authentication bypass CVE-2024-27834 as exploited on 2026-11-04

objects.description:
SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated file read, no fix will ship; replace with NSM

SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 of 2026-11-03 says an unauthenticated attacker with network access to SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier may read internal GMS files (CVE-2026-109593, CVSS 3.1 9.1), with a post-authentication SQL injection beside it (CVE-2026-109594, 6.8). The product reached end of support on 2026-09-30, so SonicWall releases no fix, names no workaround and urges migration to Network Security Manager; the advisory says nothing about exploitation.
objects.name: CVE-2026-109593 and CVE-2026-109594, SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: an unauthenticated network attacker may read internal GMS files (CVSS 3.1 9.1), and SonicWall says the end-of-life product gets no fix and has no workaround

objects.description: Microsoft (2026-11-05) reports an agentic framework searching public GitHub for OAuth application secrets from August 2026 and service-principal sign-ins with valid application credentials from 2026-10-28; Todyl (2026-11-03) reports one operator signing in as about 45 MSP application registrations since 2026-11-01 and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them, without tying it to ARTEX.
objects.name: Exposed application credentials used for Entra service-principal sign-ins (October to November 2026)

objects.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence quarterly email-threat report (2026-11-05) covering Q3 2026: tenant- and user-level overrides applied to 63% of spoofed business-service messages with a recorded security outcome in September, SVG attachments leading CAPTCHA-gated phishing, Teams impersonators moving to ordinary personal names, and a device-code phishing campaign using a QR code in a Word document.
objects.name: Microsoft Email Threat Landscape Q3 2026

objects.description: Open-source digital forensics and incident-response agent that Kaspersky saw a Storm-2603 intrusion install from a SharePoint worker process, an outdated build vulnerable to CVE-2025-6264, and use for persistence, discovery, data collection and payload execution (Kaspersky, 2026-11-05).
objects.name: Velociraptor

objects.description: Open-source HTTP forward-proxy tunnelling tool that Kaspersky saw implemented inside an in-memory SharePoint shell so that the server relayed connections from the command server into the internal network (Kaspersky, 2026-11-05).
objects.name: suo5

objects.description:
FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier: an inbound SIP MESSAGE selects the api chat proto and runs FreeSWITCH API commands; the vendor says exploitation has been observed
CVSS: 9.8 · Type: rce · Vector: zero-click · Auth: pre-auth
Affected: FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier; any SIP profile that accepts inbound MESSAGE, which stock conf/vanilla enables on the internal and external profiles
Fixed: FreeSWITCH 1.11.3, which adds a per-profile enable-chat-api-proto parameter that is off unless set
objects.name: CVE-2026-116779

objects.description:
OpenSSH Portable before 10.6p2 on musl libc without PAM (*sshole): a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to accounts whose password field is *
CVSS: 8.1 · Type: auth-bypass · Vector: zero-click · Auth: pre-auth
Affected: OpenSSH Portable before 10.6p2 on Linux with musl libc and no PAM; needs an account whose password field is * and at least one other account with a real password
Fixed: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2; Alpine edge 10.6_p2-r0, 3.24 10.3_p1-r2, 3.23 10.2_p1-r1, 3.22 10.0_p1-r11, 3.21 9.9_p2-r1, 3.20 9.7_p1-r6, 3.19 9.6_p1-r3, 3.18 9.3_p2-r4, 3.17 9.1_p1-r7, 3.16 9.0_p1-r6 per OX Security; temporary mitigation PasswordAuthentication no
objects.name: CVE-2026-123158

objects.description:
OpenSSH 10.6p2: password bypass on musl Linux without PAM (Alpine, OpenWrt); update or turn passwords off

OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and rates exploitation unknown; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. Previdian's page, as read on 2026-11-07, reports 15 exploitation attempts from 10 addresses since 2026-11-06 and, according to The Hacker News, a successful root login on an Alpine honeypot; CISA does not list the flaw.
objects.name: CVE-2026-123158, OpenSSH Portable before 10.6p2 (*sshole): on Linux with musl libc and no PAM, a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to accounts whose password field is *; NCSC Switzerland issued an advisory (CVSS 3.1 8.1)

objects.description:
FreeSWITCH: one SIP MESSAGE runs API commands, vendor says exploited; fixed in 1.11.3

SignalWire's advisory of 2026-10-28 describes CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS 3.1 9.8): an inbound SIP MESSAGE to a FreeSWITCH SIP profile selects the api chat proto and runs FreeSWITCH API commands with the privileges of the FreeSWITCH process, in the default configuration of 1.11.2 and earlier, and the advisory states that exploitation of this path has been observed in the wild. BSI CERT-Bund relayed it as a critical advisory on 2026-11-05; no source names an actor or victim, and the exploitation claim is the vendor's alone.
objects.name: CVE-2026-116779, FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier: one inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat proto and run FreeSWITCH API commands, the vendor says exploitation has been observed, and 1.11.3 fixes it (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

objects.description: Kaspersky attributes the case to Storm-2603 with moderate confidence and saw Velociraptor used for persistence, discovery and payload execution
Kaspersky saw suo5 implemented inside the SharePoint memory shell of the case it attributes to Storm-2603

Storm-2603-linked SharePoint intrusion: memory-only VirtualPathProvider shell in w3wp.exe, then Velociraptor and tunnels

Kaspersky's retrospective of a December intrusion at a customer's on-premises SharePoint server, which it attributes to Storm-2603 with moderate confidence, shows a ToolShell exploit that left no file on disk: a C# memory shell registered as an ASP.NET VirtualPathProvider inside the IIS worker process w3wp.exe, dormant until a specific User-Agent arrived, with an suo5 proxy that turned the SharePoint host into a pivot. The actor then installed an outdated Velociraptor and several tunnelling mechanisms so access outlived the worker process, and Kaspersky's endpoint product blocked the Warlock encryption attempt.
objects.name: Kaspersky reconstructs an intrusion through SharePoint ToolShell, attributed to Storm-2603 with moderate confidence, whose implant lived only inside w3wp.exe: an ASP.NET VirtualPathProvider memory shell with a suo5 tunnel, then Velociraptor, several tunnelling mechanisms and Warlock's AV killer

objects.description: Microsoft names ARTEX for the GitHub secret search; Todyl does not tie its operator to ARTEX or to any framework

Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them

Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, while Todyl does not tie its case to ARTEX and cannot say where the secrets came from.
objects.name: Exposed application credentials: Microsoft sees an agentic framework search GitHub for OAuth and cloud application secrets and then sign in as the applications from 2026-10-28, and Todyl sees an operator use MSP applications to reach 27 organisations, government clients among them

objects.description:
Microsoft Q3 email report: overrides let authentication-failing spoofed mail through; SVG CAPTCHA phishing returns

Microsoft's Q3 2026 email-threat report finds that many malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of business services were delivered despite failing authentication because tenant- or user-level overrides applied, 63% of the messages with a recorded security outcome in September. It also reports SVG attachments leading CAPTCHA-gated phishing at quarter end, Teams impersonators shifting from help-desk display names to ordinary personal names, and an August device-code phishing campaign that used a QR code in a Word document against legal organisations.
objects.name: Microsoft Email Threat Landscape Q3 2026: tenant and user overrides delivered spoofed business-service mail that failed authentication, SVG attachments return as CAPTCHA-phishing carriers, and Teams impersonators move to ordinary personal names

objects.description:
Qilin's October build spreads through vCenter and ESXi, reboots into Safe Mode and prints notes on office printers

Seqrite compares a March 2026 and an October 2026 Qilin (Agenda) sample and reports that the newer build embeds a PowerShell engine that logs in to vCenter, disables HA and DRS and pushes Linux payloads to ESXi hosts over SSH, shuts down the processes that lock files through the Windows Restart Manager instead of brute-force termination, sets a Safe Mode reboot so EDR drivers do not load, and sends ransom notes to TCP 9100 on local subnets. It is a vendor analysis of two samples with no incident confirmation.
objects.name: Seqrite: reverse engineering of two Qilin builds shows the October 2026 variant adding a vCenter and ESXi spreading engine, Restart Manager lock release, a Safe Mode reboot loop and ransom notes printed to office printers

objects.description: Agentic attack campaign that Acronis TRU attributes with high confidence to a single operator in Taiwan: a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, that over 12 observed days targeted emergency services, banks, universities and military systems in 11 countries and took patient-care and dispatch records from Taiwanese emergency services.
objects.name: BOSSAI

objects.description: Technical University of Munich incident announced 2026-11-06: attackers captured the central-login passwords of all persons who signed in to the legacy myTUM portal, used a TUMonline system administrator's credentials to attack the campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM took off the network; accounts with MFA were protected.
objects.name: TU Munich myTUM legacy portal credential capture and TUMonline attack, November 2026

objects.description: Cambodia-based, financially motivated intrusion cluster that Microsoft Threat Intelligence says primarily targets financial organizations in Southeast Asia and a smaller number of large financial organizations globally; since October 2026 it has used the agentic framework ARTEX with conventional automated tools and the WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2 remote access tools.
objects.name: Storm-3358

objects.description: Ransomware activity named BlackNevas by Kaspersky GERT in a case on an ESXi estate, October 2025, where the attacker used a reused ESXi root password reachable from a PRTG Network Monitor to run the encryptor on several hosts.
objects.name: BlackNevas

objects.description: Cantonal information-security legislation of Canton Aargau; the government council adopted the ordinance (InfoSiV) and set 1 January 2027 for the law and ordinance to enter into force, with an information-security specialist unit that is to receive directive and enforcement powers and a cyber coordination office at the cantonal police.
objects.name: Canton Aargau information-security law (InfoSiG) and ordinance (InfoSiV)

objects.description:
SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN: SAML authentication bypass for a user with alternate-method credentials (CVSS 3.1 7.1), CISA KEV 2026-11-06
CVSS: 7.1 · Type: auth-bypass · Vector: zero-click · Auth: post-auth
Affected: SonicOS 7.3.3-7015 and older (Gen7 hardware firewalls and NSv 270, 470, 870) and 8.2.2-8015 and older (Gen8 hardware firewalls and NSv XS, S, M, L), only when SAML is enabled for SSLVPN logins
Fixed: 7.3.4-7013 and higher (Gen7); 8.2.3-8015 and higher (Gen8); no workaround

objects.description:
SonicWall SonicOS management interface: permissive cross-domain policy (CVSS 3.1 8.8)
CVSS: 8.8 · Type: logic-flaw · Vector: user-interaction · Auth: pre-auth
Affected: SonicOS management interface, same Gen7 and Gen8 builds; permissive cross-domain policy that in specific conditions could potentially let a remote unauthenticated attacker perform unauthorized operations (not reported exploited)
Fixed: 7.3.4-7013 and higher (Gen7); 8.2.3-8015 and higher (Gen8)

CVSS: 7.5 · Type: dos · Vector: zero-click · Auth: pre-auth
Affected: SonicOS SSL-VPN service, same Gen7 and Gen8 builds; pre-authentication heap buffer overflow that could potentially cause an application-level denial of service (not reported exploited)
Fixed: 7.3.4-7013 and higher (Gen7); 8.2.3-8015 and higher (Gen8)

SonicWall SonicOS management interface: session validation flaw (CVSS 3.1 8.8)
CVSS: 8.8 · Type: auth-bypass · Vector: user-interaction · Auth: pre-auth
Affected: SonicOS management interface, same Gen7 and Gen8 builds; session validation flaw that in specific conditions could potentially let a remote unauthenticated attacker perform unauthorized operations (not reported exploited)

objects.name: CVE-2026-107154

objects.description:
SonicWall SSL VPN bypasses SAML MFA and CISA lists it exploited; upgrade Gen7 to 7.3.4-7013, Gen8 to 8.2.3-8015

SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0014 of 2026-11-06 fixes CVE-2026-19868, an SSLVPN authentication enforcement flaw (CVSS 3.1 7.1) that lets a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML, MFA enforced through SAML included, on Gen7 firewalls up to 7.3.3-7015 and Gen8 up to 8.2.2-8015 when SAML is enabled for SSLVPN logins. SonicWall says it investigated a report indicating potential exploitation and CISA lists the flaw as exploited; there is no workaround, and 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015 fix it.
objects.name: CVE-2026-19868, SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN: valid credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML and the MFA it enforces; SonicWall investigated a report of exploitation and CISA lists it as exploited (CVSS 3.1 7.1)

objects.description:
Brotli flaw hits Desigo CC, Industrial Edge and Mitel; Cisco lists Duo; Mitel and Common Configurator fixes pending

Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-06 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates) and Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2) and RoomOS among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.
objects.name: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens Desigo CC and Industrial Edge, Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending

objects.description: Acronis TRU: Hermes was the most prolific offensive agent in the mesh

BOSSAI AI agents took emergency-services data through open ports, public APIs and default credentials

Acronis TRU describes BOSSAI, an agentic campaign it attributes with high confidence to one operator in Taiwan: a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, that over 12 observed days targeted government emergency services, banks, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed data exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries. The confirmed emergency-services harm was patient-care records of a Taipei fire department and dispatch case records of a city 119 system; TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced and endpoints were filtered.
objects.name: Acronis TRU on BOSSAI: one operator's mesh of 12 AI agents took patient-care records and dispatch case data from Taiwanese emergency services through a legacy open port, a public API and default root credentials, and failed wherever authentication was enforced

objects.description:
Kaspersky: ESXi and Proxmox ransomware ran on a monitoring server's root password and admin notes, no VM escape

Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team describes two ransomware cases in virtualised estates. In the BlackNevas case a PRTG Network Monitor held ESXi root access and the same root password was reused across hosts, so the attacker connected over SSH, disabled the execInstalledOnly policy with esxcli, ran the encryptor and deleted logs; in the case attributed to The Gentlemen the actor found Proxmox root credentials in plaintext notes on an administrator workstation and used the VNC web socket to encrypt the cluster. Kaspersky stresses that no VM escape was needed.
objects.name: Kaspersky GERT: two ESXi and Proxmox ransomware cases in which a monitoring server's reused root password and plaintext administrator notes, not a VM escape, gave the attackers the hypervisor

objects.description:
Oneconsult: a site granted a folder in Chrome or Edge can steal tokens and plant VS Code and PowerShell persistence

Oneconsult's analysis of Chromium's Windows blocklist shows that a website granted a folder through the File System Access API after two clicks keeps a handle for as long as the tab is open, and that the blocklist leaves .vscode, .Azure, C:\Users\Public, SMB shares and, after a OneDrive Known Folder Move, the Desktop reachable. The paths it demonstrates are token and .env theft, a fake VS Code extension and PowerShell profile or module backdoors that need the Bypass or Unrestricted execution policy, and a file proxy through the open tab that EDR sees only as browser file activity.
objects.name: Oneconsult on the File System Access API: after two clicks a website holds read and write access to folders such as .vscode, .Azure, the public desktop and SMB shares in Chrome and Edge, enough for token theft and persistence without a process on the host

objects.description:
Aargau's information-security law and ordinance take effect 1 January 2027; a specialist unit is to get directive powers

The Aargau government council announced on 2026-11-06 that it adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and that the information-security law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance enter into force on 1 January 2027. An information-security specialist unit is to advise cantonal bodies with directive and enforcement powers, and a cantonal cyber coordination office, headed from that date by Bernhard Droz, and a personnel-security-vetting unit sit at the cantonal police.

external_references.source_name: Kanton Aargau, Departement Finanzen und Ressourcen (Bulletin zur Regierungsratssitzung)

objects.name: Canton Aargau adopts its information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and sets 1 January 2027 for the information-security law and ordinance, with a specialist unit to receive directive and enforcement powers and a cyber coordination office at the cantonal police

objects.description:
TUM: legacy portal harvested central-login passwords, an admin's credentials reached TUMonline; MFA accounts held

The Technical University of Munich said on 2026-11-06 that unknown attackers attacked its myTUM portal and captured the central-login passwords of all persons who had signed in there, among them the credentials of a TUMonline system administrator, with which they attacked the campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM took off the network. TUM says accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected, reported the incident to the Bavarian data-protection commissioner and filed a criminal complaint; heise reports that the entry point was a legacy system and that about 60,000 users are concerned.
objects.name: Technical University of Munich: attackers captured the central-login passwords of everyone who signed in to the legacy myTUM portal, took a TUMonline system administrator's credentials and attacked the campus-management system; accounts with MFA were protected
